title: The Real Meaning of JavaScript Scope

scenes.say: Ever wonder why some variables work everywhere, while others vanish outside a block? Let's crack JavaScript scope.

scenes.label: Scope
scenes.sub: Where a variable can be accessed in your code.
scenes.say: Scope is just where a variable can be used. It decides what you can see and change.
JavaScript hoists all variable declarations. But only var is instantly usable, set to undefined. Let and const are hoisted, but you can't touch them until their line.
Closures are functions that remember their scope. Here, inner still knows secret, even after outer has finished.
JavaScript uses lexical scope. Variables are found based on where your function is written, not where you call it.

scenes.question: Can you use let before its line?
scenes.right: No, you'll get a ReferenceError due to the temporal dead zone
scenes.say: Don't fall for this. Let and const are hoisted, but not initialized. Accessing them before their line throws a ReferenceError. That's called the temporal dead zone.
